newsitem.title: UK: No Ford UK job talks, workers meet on strikes.
newsitem.headline: No Ford UK job talks, workers meet on strikes.

text.p: Workers at the Ford Motor Co's 20 plants in Britain will hold mass meetings over the next week to decide whether to take action in protest over job cuts at Ford's Halewood plant, a union spokesman said on Friday.

Ford on Thursday announced 1,300 job losses out of a workforce of around 4,500 at Halewood in Liverpool, northwest England, which produces Escort cars for the domestic market. A spokesman for the Transport and General Workers Union -- by far the biggest in Ford's plants -- said the union was still trying to arrange talks with the company, in the hope that it would review its cost-cutting plans. But no date had been set.

The following resolution is to be put to the mass meetings: "This meeting totally rejects the company's attack on Halewood which is an attack on every Ford employee and the UK. We support the trade union side in taking all necessary measures, including a ballot for strike action, to secure the future of Halewood and for an equal investment across Europe for all locations."
The unions believe Ford plans to build the next, updated version of the Escort at factories in Germany and Spain.
Before any form of union action can take place, union members have to vote in favour at secret ballots. -- London newsroom, +44 171 542 7717
